Section 33 contains several consequential Fatal Accidents Act limitation changes: cross-reference, application extension, barred actions, and substituted action deadline.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Fatal Accidents Act cross-reference to subsection 8(3.1)
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 33(1) updates the Fatal Accidents Act reference so subsection 2(2) is subject to subsections (5) and 8(3.1).
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that subsection 2(2) is amended to include subsection 8(3.1) as a subject provision.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application barred by expired action period and one-month extension
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 33(2) substitutes a rule barring applications by persons barred from bringing an action, with a limited judicial extension if the application is close to expiry.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the substituted subsection 5(4) rule for barred applicants and limited extension of time.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Death action barred by deceased expired claim and two-year or five-year deadline
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 33(3) adds subsection 8(3.1) and substitutes subsection 8(4), creating a bar based on lapse of time and an earlier-of action deadline.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the Fatal Accidents Act amendments bar actions and set the two-year or five-year deadline.

Section 1 defines many terms used across the Marital Property Act, so the definition groups should stay tied to actual defined terms.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court, spouse, cohabit, and domestic contract definitions
proposedGroups.reason: These terms identify the adjudicative body, relationship status, cohabitation, and domestic-contract concept used in the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definitions of Court, spouse, cohabit, and domestic contract.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Marital property, family assets, household goods, and marital home definitions
proposedGroups.reason: These terms define the main property categories used in marital property division and possession rules.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definitions of marital property, family assets, household goods, and marital home.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Business asset, marital debts, net proceeds, property, and disposition definitions
proposedGroups.reason: These terms define assets, debts, proceeds, property, and transfers relevant to property division and transactions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definitions of business asset, marital debts, net proceeds, property, and disposition.

reason: Section 2 treats child care, household management, and financial provision as joint responsibilities of equal importance for contributions, shares, and debts.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Joint responsibilities and equal sharing premise
proposedGroups.reason: Section 2 treats child care, household management, and financial provision as joint responsibilities of equal importance for contributions, shares, and debts.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how joint responsibilities support equal shares of marital property and equal burdens of marital debts.

reason: Section 3 covers entitlement to equal division, the 60-day application limit, deemed spouse status after nullity, and extension grounds.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Equal division triggers for marital property
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 3(1) lists the circumstances in which a spouse may apply for equal division of marital property.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the divorce, nullity, separation, and marriage-breakdown triggers for equal division.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Sixty-day limit after ceasing to be a spouse
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 3(2) sets the 60-day limit after divorce or declaration of nullity, subject to extension.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the 60-day application limit applies.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Nullity deemed-spouse rule and extension grounds
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 3(3) and 3(4) address deemed spouse status after nullity and grounds for extending the limitation period.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how nullity affects spouse status and when the Court may extend the application period.

reason: Section 4 is a multi-part surviving-spouse scheme covering entitlement, deadlines, estate administration, elections, and limits on multiple remedies.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Surviving spouse entitlement and vesting of home goods
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 4(1) through 4(3) establish the surviving spouse application entitlement, vesting possibility, and court powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the surviving spouse entitlement to equal division and possible vesting of the marital home and household goods.

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 4(4), 4(8), and 4(9) set service and application timing rules related to estate administration.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the timing and service rules for surviving spouse property division applications.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Election and no double recovery rules
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 4(5), 4(6), 4(7), and 4(10) address elections, barred applications, testamentary acceptance, and limits on combining claims.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how section 4 controls elections and prevents overlapping surviving-spouse property claims.

reason: Section 5 states when property division applications may continue by or against estates and when Survival of Actions Act does not apply.
